clue.text: Cover to protect an antique sofa

indicators.note: the cover is set around the next word to shelter it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cape is a cloak, a garment that covers

explanation.surface: Someone throws a dust sheet over a valuable old settee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' reads as a dust sheet thrown over furniture, but it is the cloak; the definition is the old French couch, not the party snack sharing its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is also an eighteenth-century French couch, a period piece of furniture.

clue.text: In front sections of charity shop you'll find a gent's old clothes perhaps

indicators.note: the letter A is found sitting between the two initials, so it goes inside them
the front section of each of these two words is its opening letter

parts.note: a toff is a well-dressed gentleman, and the possessive 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: A gentleman's old clothes are on sale near the front of a charity shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front' says the CAS made from the initials around A comes before TOFF'S. A toff is British slang for an upper-class gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments discarded by an owner, such as those given to second-hand shops, are known by this name.

clue.text: Downfall of Meissen works

indicators.note: the letters of the word are worked over, reshaped into a different order

explanation.surface: The collapse of a famous German porcelain factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Meissen is a German porcelain maker, so 'works' looks like a factory; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: One's nemesis is the agent of ruin, a downfall that seems deserved or inevitable.

clue.text: Gloomy atmosphere for the family in a dark London theatre

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud or mood hanging over things

indicators.note: the family-film letter sits inside the word for dark

parts.note: dim means dark, poorly lit
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, family viewing

explanation.surface: A dark London theatre has a gloomy feel for families who visit.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal viewing. The London Palladium is a famous West End variety theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palladium is a well-known playhouse in London's West End, home to variety shows and musicals.

clue.text: Printout of chapter at start of work penned by novelist

indicators.note: something penned by a writer is enclosed by the writer's name here

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist

indicators.note: the chapter letter is placed at the front of the next piece

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A printout of a chapter from the start of a work by a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper copy of a document is the physical printed output, as opposed to an on-screen version.

clue.text: After a day's work, do drink a sherry

indicators.note: the word for do is placed after everything that comes before it in the clue

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday, a day
to till is to work the soil
a do is a fuss, which is also an ado

explanation.surface: After a day's work, someone is urged to have a glass of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is a noun here, a fuss; 'drink' simply joins the wordplay to the definition. The blog prefers DO with an unclued extra A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a type of medium-dry Spanish sherry, darker than fino.

clue.text: Attractive group of Swedish yuppies

indicators.note: group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Young Scandinavian professionals considered good-looking as a set.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British for good-looking, sexy.

clue.text: Collection of writings piled up by editor's assistant in a short time

indicators.note: in a down entry, piling up means the letters are stacked from the bottom, so they read upwards

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor, who helps an editor
a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Books stacked by a sub-editor in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' turns SUB+IN+MO to read OMNIBUS from the bottom of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition is a volume gathering several works by one author into one book.

clue.text: Dog has a turn after eating a plant

indicators.note: the word for dog swallows the letter A, so it goes inside
turning the whole result round means it is read backwards

parts.note: to worry is to harass, as a dog worries sheep, and both words mean to pester persistently

explanation.surface: A dog turns round after eating something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after eating' puts A inside WORRY to make WORRAY; 'has a turn' turns that round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow, or milfoil, is a white-flowered wild herb of the daisy family.

clue.text: Language very much associated with African country

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so kind'
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A language strongly linked with a country in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Somali is the Cushitic tongue spoken in Somalia and the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Is one making appearance in dock before being given time?

definitions.text: Is one making appearance in dock before being given time?

indicators.note: the first two words show up inside the harbour word
the harbour word as it was before the time letter was added, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a port is a harbour where ships dock

explanation.surface: Asks whether a defendant stands in court before being sentenced to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT before 'time' (T) is added is POR; IS ONE appears inside it. The whole clue also describes a murderer awaiting sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer by toxic substance stands trial in the dock and is then sentenced to a prison term.

clue.text: Attack by lawless leader waving a shotgun about

indicators.note: the gun is waved around, so its letters are thrown into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An outlaw chief brandishes a shotgun in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: L (lawless leader) and A SHOTGUN are rearranged together; 'waving' signals it and 'about' adds to the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce assault, a violent charge.

clue.text: Ornamental style developed in big garden, planted with principally

clue.text: Hello and bye-bye, nasty one

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Hello and bye-bye, nasty one (5)', gives YO + BB but no clue word supplies the final O; a word (perhaps 'old') looks lost in OCR, and no scan or search gives the printed text.

clue.text: Trendy dressers love wearing flash panties when partying

indicators.note: the shuffled underwear is worn by the love letter, so it goes inside
the panties are flung about at a party, so their letters are mixed up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Fashionable people show off flashy knickers at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when partying' mixes FLASH PANTIES into FASHI-NPLATES; 'wearing' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion plate was originally an illustration of the latest styles, then a person who dresses stylishly.

clue.text: Keen worker goes to bottom of ditch

indicators.note: in a down entry, the bottom is the end, so this piece follows the ditch

parts.note: a trench is a long ditch
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A keen labourer climbs down to the bottom of a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and sharp, like a keen blade or keen wit.

clue.text: Rather clever, having answer to clue filled in

indicators.note: the answer word is filled into the clever word, so it goes inside

parts.note: sly means cunning, clever
a light is a crossword term for the answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone is rather clever, having completed a crossword answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'light' is solvers' jargon for a grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly and rather both mean to a small degree, somewhat.

clue.text: Moody office worker takes time out to lunch

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
an era is a period of time
out to lunch is slang for crazy, mental

explanation.surface: A moody office employee takes time off to go out for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' reads as a lunch break, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone temperamental is volatile, given to sudden changes of mood.

clue.text: Given job, repaired one tank

indicators.note: the tank is fixed by putting its parts back in a different order

explanation.surface: A mechanic gets work after fixing a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken on is to be hired, employed.

clue.text: Mostly knitted material on navy headgear

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: tricot is a knitted fabric
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A hat made mostly of knitted fabric, worn in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the two parts, the second below the first in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat, worn by naval officers of old.

clue.text: Father left wearing cotton, perhaps

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
to be in something is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: Dad left the house in cotton clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplin is a plain-woven fabric, typically made of cotton, so cotton is one example of it.

clue.text: Bits of old rope for use on ship? Nonsense, we 'ear

definitions.text: Bits of old rope for use on ship?

indicators.note: how the word sounds when spoken by someone who drops the H, as the apostrophe in 'ear shows

parts.note: hokum is nonsense, bunkum

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of old rope being useful on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we 'ear' imitates a Cockney dropping the H, so HOKUM sounds like OAKUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre picked from old ropes, used for caulking a vessel's seams.

clue.text: Game shot during Christmas season

indicators.note: the answer occurs during the two words, in the middle of them

explanation.surface: Something was shot during the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game shot' suggests a pheasant shoot; it is a billiards stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A massé is a billiards stroke made with a steeply angled cue to swerve the ball.

clue.text: Making reference to relative's suffering

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative
aching means in pain, suffering

explanation.surface: Someone mentions that a relative is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it, bring it up in talk.

clue.text: He painted country view next to river

parts.note: land means a country
to see is to view

explanation.surface: An artist painted a rural scene beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Edwin Landseer painted animals and sculpted the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian English artist famous for animal pictures such as The Monarch of the Glen.

clue.text: Floor arrangement?

explanation.surface: A question about how a room is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: To floor someone is to knock them down; the clue reads as a floor plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out is to knock someone flat, to floor them; a layout is a design or arrangement.

clue.text: Game plan accepted by small number

indicators.note: the plan is accepted, taken in, by the number, so it goes inside

parts.note: no., short for number, is a small abbreviation
to intend is to plan

explanation.surface: A game plan approved by a handful of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is a games brand, the Japanese console maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is a Japanese company making video games and consoles.

clue.text: Mean scam ending in tragedy

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a scam

indicators.note: the ending of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cruel con trick ends in tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means tight-fisted, miserly with money.
